cards.text: For chapters now, the writer of Chronicles has been listing family after family (1 Chronicles 1-8), and here he wraps it up: all Israel was recorded in the genealogies written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. Then comes the hard news. Judah was exiled to Babylon.

cards.question: The writer tells us why. Judah was exiled to Babylon because of their ___.
But the story doesn't end in Babylon. People are moving back onto their own property in their cities. Who are among the first to resettle?

cards.text: Some of the people of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim and Manasseh settle in Jerusalem itself. Then comes the roll call: families from Judah and Benjamin, then the priests, then the Levites. The Benjamites come with 956 relatives, and the priests with 1,760, all able men for the work of the service of the house of God.

Next come the gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman and their relatives, with Shallum as their chief. Shallum and his relatives from the Korahites are assigned to guard the thresholds of the Tent.

cards.question: True or false: guarding is a brand new job for Shallum's family, because their fathers never had it.

cards.text: Way back, Phinehas son of Eleazar, a priest and Aaron's grandson (Exodus 6:25), was in charge of the gatekeepers. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, and I would have PAID for a gatekeeper deciding what got tossed in on top of me.

cards.question: What does the writer say about Phinehas, who was once in charge of the gatekeepers?

cards.text: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah keeps the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. All told, 212 men are chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds, registered by genealogy in their villages.

cards.question: David, Israel's king, and Samuel the seer had appointed the gatekeepers to their positions of ___.

cards.text: So the gatekeepers and their descendants guard the gates of the house of the LORD, the house called the Tent. Same family, same doors, generation after generation, friend, like a family bakery that never changes the locks.

cards.question: Where around the house of the LORD are the gatekeepers stationed?

cards.text: The four chief gatekeepers, who are Levites, are trusted with the rooms and the treasuries of the house of God. Their relatives come in from the villages at fixed times to serve with them.

cards.question: When the gatekeepers' relatives come in from the villages, how long do they serve at a time?

cards.text: Night falls, and those four chief gatekeepers don't clock out. They spend the night stationed all around the house of God.

cards.question: Why do the four chief gatekeepers spend the night around the house of God?

answers.text: They guard it and open it each morning
They have no homes of their own
They are fasting for the feast

cards.question: True or false: the men put in charge of the articles used in worship count them whenever they're brought in or taken out.

cards.text: Others look after the sanctuary's furnishings, plus the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense and spices, and some of the priests' sons mix the spices. Then a Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, gets a job that makes my mustache stand STRAIGHT up.

cards.question: What is Mattithiah the Levite entrusted with?

cards.text: Some Kohathites, a Levite clan, prepare the rows of the showbread every Sabbath. Then there are the musicians, heads of Levite families who stay in the temple chambers, and they're excused from other duties.

cards.question: Why are the musicians exempt from other duties?

answers.text: They are on duty day and night
Their families serve in their place

cards.text: All these heads of Levite families live in Jerusalem. Then the writer lists one more family, the family of Jeiel the father of Gibeon, and a big name shows up: Kish was the father of Saul, the man the people made king of Israel (1 Samuel 11:15). From Saul's son Jonathan, the line runs all the way down to Azel and his six sons.
